title: Jacob's pillar versus the pillars of his opponents
english: It is clear, then, that he assumes two kinds of pillars. For he would not have accepted Jacob's pillar with approval while rebuking those of his opponents as impiously erected. Those pillars imprint demonic phantoms of idolatry with impious belief, but the pillar of the forefather Jacob does not display the same activity as those. For the righteous man, having been inspired by the Holy Spirit, first sees the very bodily form of Christ being vividly pre-painted beforehand, which is visible and subject to local circumscription. Second, he also depicts the victory-bearing trophy of the cross, likened in a manner resembling a ladder. For by this it was also firmly set on high, drawing all people to itself.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The author is opening his treatise by distinguishing Jacob's pillar at Bethel from the pillars of Jacob's opponents, arguing that Jacob's was a prophecy of Christ and the cross.
